[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Binary Subarrays With Sum** [LC 930 · Binary Subarrays With Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-subarrays-with-sum/){difficulty="Medium"}

Here the object being counted is a window, and the predicate is a statement about its **sum**. There are two well-separated ways to stop enumerating windows, and both are worth owning, because they cover different generalisations.

**Route 1 — turn windows into pairs.** A window sum is a difference of prefix sums (@sec-pref-def): $\text{sum}(i..j) = pre_j - pre_{i-1}$, so "window equals $goal$" becomes "a **pair** of prefix sums differing by $goal$". Fix the right end $j$, whose prefix value is $pre$; the window is good exactly when some earlier prefix equals $pre - goal$. That is once more the right-end tally of @sec-cnt-p2-goodpairs, with prefix sums as the currency: keep a table of how many times each prefix value has occurred and add `cnt[pre - goal]` per step. The table must be seeded with `cnt[0] = 1`, because the empty prefix at position $-1$ is the partner of every window that starts at slot $0$. On the sample the prefix values are $1,1,2,2,3$ and the lookups are $-1,-1,0,0,1$ with table counts $0,0,1,1,2$ — charges $0,0,1,1,2$ that add to $4$.

**Route 2 — count a superset and subtract.** "Exactly $goal$" is awkward for a window; "**at most** $goal$" is not, because $nums$ is non-negative: as the right end advances the window sum only grows, so the smallest `left` that keeps the sum $\le goal$ is monotone, and every start in $[left, right]$ is also valid — the number of subarrays ending at $right$ is just $right - left + 1$. Summing those gives $atMost(goal)$. Now write the hard count as a difference of two easy ones (@sec-sw-a4, @sec-cnt-a4):

$$\text{exactly } goal \;=\; atMost(goal) - atMost(goal-1),$$

because a window with sum $\le goal$ either has sum exactly $goal$ or sum $\le goal-1$, and the two classes are counted by the same sweeping code with a different budget. On the sample $atMost(2) = 14$ (all but the one window of sum $3$), $atMost(1) = 10$, and $14 - 10 = 4$ — the sample answer, and the per-right charges $1,2,3,4,4$ visible in the storyboard below.

Route 1 works for any integer array (it is LC 560 verbatim, negative values included) at $O(n)$ with an $O(n)$ table. Route 2 needs non-negative values and pays only $O(1)$ space. Neither is "the" answer — they are the two halves of the toolbox.

[Solved in full in @sec-cnt-p3-binsum.]{.card-link}
